lines.x: Sri Lankan shares fell 0.8% on Friday to log their worst weekly decline in six months after the central bank unexpectedly raised its key policy rate by 25 basis points.
The Sri Lankan rupee was quoted at 332.75/85 to the US dollar in spot trade.
Fitch Ratings forecasts Sri Lanka's government debt will fall to about 92% of GDP in 2026 from 115% in 2022, still well above the 55% median for B-rated sovereigns.
Sri Lanka's inflation is expected to remain elevated in the near term, reaching around 9% by month-end, according to the central bank governor.
